title: The “AI” in GlobalQuantAI is actually mostly maths 😂
author: Even_Calligrapher906
selftext:
One thing I find funny about building GlobalQuantAI is that people see the words AI signal and probably assume I'm throwing some expensive LLM at the market every 15 seconds 😂

Nah.

The actual signal is mostly maths.

It looks at stuff like RSI, MACD, EMA, Bollinger Bands, Stochastic, volume and price behaviour across different timeframes, then combines those readings into the UP / DOWN / HOLD signal and confidence score.

The wording you see underneath is basically a template that explains what the numbers are saying, which is the part I call the “AI signal”.

Honestly I did it this way because paying for an AI API every time the market updates would get stupid expensive, especially when the AI can still be wrong 

anyway 

So the expensive part isn't pretending a model can predict the market. The useful part is getting the calculations right and presenting them in a way that's actually understandable.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
honestly the maths-not-LLM part is the sane choice, the bit I'd push on is the confidence score. RSI, MACD, stochastic and Bollinger all read the same price series, so when five of them agree that is one vote counted five times, not high confidence. the only way that number means anything is scoring it against what happened next, per bucket, for a few months.

that scoring step is the one people skip, which is why I built Quantradin: the signal runs on paper, every UP and DOWN gets a measured fill and a grade, no money involved. no cost, paper only, and my profile has the rest should you feel like running yours through it.
